decision: Worktree Isolation v0 jumps the queue ahead of Plan D (2026-06-08-004, paused pre-lock at its D007) per operator direction 2026-06-10. v0 is a platform primitive: isolation + honesty about who is where — nothing clever.
rationale: Operator: the recent pain (long-lived branches, plan drafts on different bases, cleanup commits, stale stashes, untracked duplicates, merge/close rituals, multiple sessions on one repo state) is exactly the risk profile of Plan D + 008 + Plan B + C+ overlapping. Live demonstration the same day: switching branches to draft THIS plan reverted Plan D's freshly-edited artifacts in the shared tree.

decision: Binding registry lives at $DONTPANIC_HOME/worktrees.json (install-level, mirroring projects_registry.py: Pydantic v2 extra=forbid, degrade-to-empty+WARN), NOT in tracked plan-dir files. Gate-time snapshots (F002) and override records (F003) DO land in the plan's audit evidence because they are point-in-time facts about a gate run.
rationale: A binding recorded in tracked files would itself conflict across worktrees — the exact failure mode this plan removes. Separation follows the operator-config-separation principle: registry = runtime install state; evidence = audit trail.

decision: owner_actor in v0 is informational only: $DONTPANIC_ACTOR env if set, else user@host. It is recorded and rendered, never enforced. Leases/claims are explicitly out of scope.
rationale: Keep v0 tight; enforcement semantics (lease expiry, steal, multi-agent contention) need real-world signal first — demand-driven scoping.

decision: No force-removal path exists anywhere in v0: deleting a dirty worktree requires the operator to use raw git deliberately. plan close never auto-removes; it may only print the explicit remove command.
rationale: Dirty/untracked state has repeatedly turned out to hold value (or hazards) worth a human look — e.g. Finder-duplicate hazards and deliberately-unmerged work found this week. Fail closed; cleanup is explicit and audited.

decision: Round-1 sufficiency findings (5) resolved by tightening, not overriding: (1) F006 pins base selection — default = repo default branch resolved to a SHA, never the invoking checkout's HEAD implicitly; --base explicit + recorded; unresolvable base refuses. (2) The directive's 'build' path = orchestrate dispatch — added to F002's recording set AND F003's guarded set. (3) plan audit added to F003's guarded set (it writes evidence). (4) DontPanic has NO merge command — merging to main is the operator's external gh ritual (enforce_admins-toggle bypass), so the guarded {lock, audit, close, disposition, dispatch} set IS the complete plan-mutating surface; recorded here so the contract path is named, not implied. (5) F007 now requires a DOM-level render test through the real dashboard page module, not just a payload block.
rationale: All five were plan-level coverage gaps in MY draft against the operator's directive, not new scope. One considered pass per the paid-gate cadence rule.

decision: Round-2 sufficiency findings (2 high / 3 med, branch b_high_severity — round 1 cleared 100%) resolved by pinning: (1) binding schema gains base_sha (resolved commit SHA, pinned at create, never recomputed) distinct from base_ref, and the worktree is created AT base_sha; (2) repo_root derives authoritatively from the plan dir's containing repository, never the invoking checkout (wrong-invoking-repo test); (3) broken-binding includes path-is-not-a-worktree-OF-recorded-repo_root (membership check); (4) F007 wires the REAL dashboard state producer, fixture tests alone insufficient; (5) derivation pinned — path $DONTPANIC_HOME/worktrees/<repo-dir-name>/<plan-id>, branch plan/<plan-id>, pre-existing branch refuses in v0.
rationale: Second considered pass. All five were pinnable cells, two at high severity (un-dispositionable by design). If round 3 surfaces another fresh layer, STOP and surface the matrix-enumeration pattern to the operator with the rounds ledger instead of a fourth paid call.

decision: STOPPED at round 3 per D006's stop rule and the operator's paid-gate cadence — NO fourth paid lock call without an operator decision. Rounds ledger: r1 = 5 findings (2H/3M, branch d_first_round) -> 100% cleared by D005; r2 = 5 NEW (2H/3M, b_high_severity) -> 100% cleared by D006; r3 = 4 NEW (1H/3M, b_high_severity: snapshot omits base_sha, not-inside-any-worktree refusal unpinned, branch-drift parity HIGH, removal audit lacks removed_by). All four r3 findings were folded into the plan text offline (free) in this commit. The plan is tightened through three layers; every round cleared its predecessor and surfaced the next layer of pin-class cells — the same enumeration shape C0 hit (its D017).
rationale: Severity trumps class, so the r3 high is un-dispositionable under policy v1.0; policy v1.1 (streak-gated high-pin dispositions, plan 2026-06-10-001) is drafted but demand-gated. Operator options, mirroring C0 D017: (a) one more paid re-lock against the now-tightened plan; (b) ledger-justified recorded override (--ignore-sufficiency-findings) citing three 100%-clearance rounds of auditor-classed pins, all already addressed in text; (c) treat this as the second real instance demanded by the v1.1 trigger and lock under the new policy after it ships.

decision: Round-4 (first under policy v1.1, streak=3, 100% clearance again) resolved per the operator fork rule: the HIGH was auditor-classed plan_contract — a REAL fail-open hole in my draft (degrade-to-empty registry + unbound passthrough composes so a corrupt worktrees.json silently disables wrong-worktree protection) — so TIGHTEN, not disposition: corrupt registry now FAILS CLOSED for all guarded entry points (distinct registry-corrupt refusal) while read-only renderers degrade with a visible warning. Also pinned: F005 refuses every unhealthy binding before removal (missing/non-worktree/wrong-repo/detached/drifted, named health check); F007 adds the branch-drifted fixture across all three renderers; F006 pins the default-branch resolution rule (origin/HEAD -> local main-over-master -> refuse).
rationale: Exactly the v1.1 design intent: plan_contract highs stay hard work; the matrix_pin med/low would have been disposition-eligible under the streak but were trivial to pin alongside.

decision: Round-5 findings (1 high implementation_detail / 2 med / 1 med scope_guard, full clearance again, streak=4) tightened: (1) create AND remove use the strict registry load — fail closed on corrupt registry before mutating registry or filesystem (consequence-completion of D008's contract); (2) registry_corrupt warning flag on the status model + corrupt-registry fixture across all three renderers; (3) untracked_count pinned to porcelain default-mode entries (collapsed dir = 1, fixture-asserted); (4) F003 now OWNS the no-merge-command guard with a CLI-surface test. NOTE for the policy ledger: the high was auditor-classed implementation_detail — correctly NOT streak-eligible under v1.1 (only matrix_pin is) — a third fork case beyond the operator's two; trivially tightenable so tightened. If round 6 surfaces another fresh high, STOP and surface.
rationale: Each round's findings remain responsive to the previous edit (consequence-findings, not enumeration); severity tail is thinning.

decision: OPERATOR-DIRECTED final structural pass (round 6, 1 high wiring_gap + 3 med, full clearance again): replaced the piecemeal guard/remove conditions with ONE canonical binding_health predicate (exists AND is_git_worktree AND belongs_to_recorded_repo_root AND on_recorded_branch; probe errors/indeterminate = unhealthy, fail closed; machine-readable failed-conjunct reason) owned by F004 and CALLED — never re-specified — by every plan-mutating guard (F003) and by removal eligibility (F005). This closes the class the last three highs were instances of (each poked a missing conjunct of the same predicate). Also: override path STILL captures the binding snapshot (combined test, F002/F003); unhealthy bindings render explicit null dirty/untracked_count with the health reason, consistently across list/brief/dashboard (F004/F007). POST-LOCK FORK (operator): clears or med/low pins -> proceed (dispositions); another fresh high in the guard/threat-model area -> STOP and split F003/F005 into a dedicated hardening plan; a high outside the isolation predicate -> judge normally.
rationale: Operator: the r6 high is core to the isolation primitive, not polish — path+branch equality is insufficient if the path is no longer a worktree of the recorded repo_root. Worktree isolation is foundational enough to warrant this final structural tightening before any override consideration.

decision: Round-7 findings (2 high integration_gap / 4 med, full clearance, ZERO findings in the guard/threat-model area — the D010 binding_health pass closed that class) judged normally per the operator fork (highs are in a NEW area: create/remove lifecycle atomicity): (1) create writes the binding ONLY after git success and best-effort rolls back worktree+branch on registry-write failure (invariant: nothing outlives the command unbound); (2) remove is audit-first — the entry is appended and flushed BEFORE any destructive step, unwritable log = no removal (unaudited cleanup impossible by construction); (3) the F007 corrupt-registry parity finding was CORRECT — my round-5/6 chained replaces had silently no-op'd; F007's fixture clause rewritten wholesale to six states (clean/dirty/broken/drifted/unhealthy-with-reason/corrupt-registry) across all three renderers; (4) guard path comparison canonicalized (realpath both sides); (5) removal cleanliness pinned: gitignored files do not block and are deleted (regenerable by declaration), nested non-submodule .git dirs block with path reported; (6) base option spelling pinned to the objective contract's dash-dash-base.
rationale: PROCESS NOTE: this is the second silent partial-edit incident (after v1.1 r4) — chained str.replace plan edits must be verified by re-reading the field, not assumed. The two highs are classic transactional pins, judged normally; if the NEXT round returns a fresh high anywhere, stop — guard-area highs split F003/F005 into a hardening plan per the operator tree, and at 8 rounds any other fresh high also warrants a stop-and-surface rather than more paid rounds.

decision: SPLIT per the operator decision tree: round 8 returned a fresh HIGH (plan_contract f-330122e8396e — whether gitignored files fall under the contract's never-delete-untracked language) in the cleanup area, so paid rounds STOP and F003 (wrong-worktree refusal) + F005 (safe cleanup) move wholesale, with their fully-hardened text, to plan 2026-06-11-001-feat-worktree-guard-hardening (draft; pre-lock design pass required; carries r8's high + the evidence-durability med as explicit design inputs). v0 is now the SUBSTRATE slice: F001 registry, F002 gate-time snapshots (override interplay deferred to the guard plan), F004 binding_health predicate + status model (exported for the guard plan to CALL), F006 create (now at a repo-key-qualified path — r8's collision med folded in: <repo-dir-name>-<short-hash-of-repo_root>), F007 visibility. Ledger at split: 8 rounds, 100% clearance each, counts 5,5,4,4,4,4,6,3; highs were all REAL and all distinct (fail-open registry, fail-closed completeness, swapped-repo, create rollback, audit ordering, cleanup contract semantics).
rationale: Operator: worktree isolation is foundational; the gate kept finding real holes, which means the guard needed a threat-model design pass, not more incremental acceptance edits. One lock of the REDUCED v0 follows — a materially smaller plan, not a continuation of the hardening rounds.

decision: Round-9 (first lock of the REDUCED substrate plan) findings were split residue, fixed: (1) HIGH — F002's gate/dispatch evidence paths now load the registry STRICTLY and refuse on a corrupt file before any side effect (moving fail-closed out with F003 had left evidence capture able to mistake corruption for no-binding); (2) F006 validates the resolved target path lies OUTSIDE repo_root and its worktrees (DONTPANIC_HOME-inside-repo cannot undermine isolation); (3) rollback semantics disambiguated — registry-write-last makes no-binding-without-worktree the HARD invariant, rollback of worktree/branch is best-effort with non-zero exit naming any residue. ONE re-lock follows; any fresh high after this = hard stop and surface.
rationale: Completing the D012 split surgery, not a new spiral — all three findings were direct consequences of the feature moves.

decision: HARD STOP per D013: round 10 returned a fresh HIGH (implementation_detail f-1cc431c80ce2 — atomic registry writes preserving pre-existing entries; not matrix_pin, so v1.1's streak valve does not apply). Both round-10 findings folded into plan text in this commit (atomic temp-then-rename writes with a kill-mid-write fixture; current_branch rendered alongside recorded branch for drifted bindings in brief+dashboard). SUBSTRATE LEDGER AT STOP: 10 rounds total (8 pre-split + 2 post-split), 100% clearance EVERY round, final counts 3,2, every finding through round 10 addressed in text. Operator decides: (a) 11th lock against the folded text; (b) ledger-justified whole-plan override — now the strongest case yet (all findings addressed, enforcement half already split out, substrate surface is low-risk: registry+create+observability, no removal command); (c) any other restructure.
rationale: Honoring the recorded stop rule matters more than the marginal confidence of an 11th round; the post-impl codex audit remains ahead as an independent code-grounded check either way.

decision: LOCKED at round 11 — CLEAN (0 findings). The operator authorized a recorded override with a precise reason (ten rounds, 100% clearance each; enforcement split out; remaining scope non-destructive substrate; implementation must prove atomic registry writes, strict load/fail-closed, create rollback, repo-qualified paths, outside-repo validation, and status rendering through tests, followed by post-impl audit) — but the mandatory pre-override regeneration (the D008-class friction: inputs had changed, so the auditor re-ran) returned ZERO findings against the round-10-folded text, so the gate passed on its own merits and the override was never consumed. status: draft -> active. Implementation burden stands exactly as the operator phrased it regardless of which path unlocked the gate.
rationale: Recorded for ledger honesty: the plan converged naturally at round 11; the override authorization existed but was not needed.
